title: Steal These Ideas: 10 CSR Activities and Gifts From IMEX and Beyond
summary: Giving back has become the norm on the convention floor, and these 10 options were inspired by IMEX America.

title: The AI Paradox Looming Over the Meetings Industry
summary: AI may turn out to be the best demand driver meetings have had in years. But attendees will increasingly discover events through chatbots, plan their schedules with AI, and arrive accustomed to digital interactions. Delivering the human connection they seek could prove harder than the industry assumes.

title: One Woman Leader on the Importance of Curiosity
summary: The new interim CEO of the incentive industry’s major association, SITE, Rebecca Wright will initially focus on questioning, listening, and learning.

title: At IMEX America, Optimism Comes With a Price Tag
summary: IMEX America proved the meetings industry still wants to gather. The question heading into 2027 is how much organizations will pay for the privilege.

title: EIC’s Plan to Help Planners Find New Job Opportunities
summary: The Events Industry Council’s new Pathways initiative aims to create new opportunities for the entire industry — from entry-level professionals to senior-level leaders. It comes at a time when many planners worry that their current skills will be obsolete within the next few years.

title: Why Networking Receptions Stress Attendees Out — And What to Build Instead
summary: Planners often treat networking as time to fill. A design strategist argues it’s a job to be done, and that the fix is giving attendees a reason to talk that isn’t networking.

title: Why a Destination-Wide Strategy Matters for Large-Scale Conferences
summary: Destination choice can have a profound impact on the legacy success of mission-led international conferences. The Melbourne Convention Bureau used its destination-wide network to support Women Deliver 2026 in furthering progressive policies and inspiring multi-million-dollar funding commitments.

title: 5 Key Statistics About the State of Incentive Programs
summary: Disruption has become the norm as incentive planners brace for continued uncertainty in 2027.

title: Some Event Line Items Have Increased By 146% Since 2019
summary: Inflation is slowing, but event pricing isn’t turning around, according to a new price index from Maritz. Planners who keep cutting last year’s program to fit this year’s budget will lose on both cost and experience.

title: What If AI Thinks Your Event Is Canceled?
summary: New research from Freeman shows that one in five attendees now uses AI to find conferences. Will it be able to find the right information about yours?
